subject: geography
title: Regeneration & Rebranding
meta_desc: A-Level Geography adventure on UK regeneration, rebranding and stakeholder conflict.
final_note: Regeneration changes both fabric and meaning of places.

concepts.def: Long-term improvement: economic, social, environmental, physical.
Reshaping place identity to attract investment, tourists or residents.
Iconic development to spark wider change; e.g. Tate Modern, Bilbao Guggenheim.
Anyone with interest in regeneration: residents, businesses, council, developers.
Displacement of original residents by wealthier incomers.
Active promotion via branding (e.g. I Love NY, GREAT Britain).

walkthroughs.body_html: LDDC (1981-1998) transformed 22 km^2 of derelict docks into Canary Wharf financial district. 120000 new jobs created; £8.7 billion private investment leveraged. Critics note displacement of working-class East End community and limited benefit to original residents.

MediaCity UK (2007-) attracted BBC (4400 staff relocated from London 2011) and ITV. Generated 7000+ jobs; rebranded Salford Quays from post-industrial to digital media hub. Lowry Centre is cultural flagship. Local residents debate access to new jobs.

Heygate Estate (Elephant & Castle, Southwark): 1200 social homes demolished; Lendlease redevelopment delivered only 82 social rented units. Original residents priced out. Illustrates how regeneration can deepen inequality without strong affordable housing requirements.

mcqs.q: BBC staff relocated to Salford MediaCity in 2011:

options: Gentrification means the city becomes more polluted as it grows.
The process by which wealthier residents move into a previously low-income urban area, raising property prices and often displacing original residents.
GDP measures the total wealth of every individual in a country.
Gentrification is when the government rebuilds an old part of the city.

mcqs.q: Why is GDP per capita a poor measure of wellbeing?
options: GDP measures economic activity, not wellbeing. It ignores inequality, unpaid work, environmental damage and quality of life — high GDP can coexist with poor health, education or happiness.
A high GDP per capita means citizens are happy and well off.
GDP measures the total wealth of every individual in a country.
Gentrification means the city becomes more polluted as it grows.

mcqs.q: Why is HDI a better measure of development than GNI per capita?
options: HDI combines income, life expectancy and education, capturing quality of life — GNI per capita is just average income and hides inequality and non-economic wellbeing.
Gentrification means the city becomes more polluted as it grows.
Because HDI measures how happy people are.
Because HDI is easier to calculate than GNI.
